problems.title: The implemented histogram is not the full-interval EoD
problems.source_location: Appendix S2.2, PDF p.16; current evaluation_utils.py, run_sbc_save_results
claim: The paper defines \(E=\int_0^1|F(\alpha)-\alpha|\,d\alpha\). Current code chooses its histogram range from observed ranks and averages boundary errors.
analysis: Take ten normalized ranks, five \(0.49\) and five \(0.51\). The empirical CDF is \(0\), then \(1/2\), then \(1\). Exact integration gives \(0.12005+0.00005+0.00005+0.12005=0.2402\). With thirty bins over the observed interval \([0.49,0.51]\), the released boundary mean is approximately \(0.0361290\); refining bins approaches \(0.005\), omitting both major tails. The exact input can arise as ranks \(49,51\) among \(100\) posterior samples.
result: The current computation does not generally evaluate or converge to the specified metric. It does not prove any published posterior is miscalibrated or any model ranking reverses.
repair: Integrate the actual empirical CDF over breakpoints including \(0,1\). On each constant-CDF interval use antiderivative \(\tfrac12(\alpha-c)|\alpha-c|\), retaining all tails and repeated ranks.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is retained where stated; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a local implementation or interpretation defect; damage to the central empirical result has not been established.

problems.title: The current author release already uses a consistent Gaussian base law
problems.source_location: Current base_distributions.py covariance paths; historical official supplement
claim: The older supplement used training covariance \(c(K+\delta I)\) and generation covariance \(cK+\delta I\). The current author-main code uses the latter consistently.
analysis: The historical difference was \(\delta(1-c)I\), nonzero for \(c\ne1\). Fresh current source places jitter outside the scalar normalization in construction, training sampling and distribution creation, so the two Gaussian covariance formulas now coincide for each fixed supported position set. The README directs publication reproduction to a separate branch because baseline-library dependencies changed; historical experiment provenance remains distinct.
result: The old supplement discrepancy is not a current error. Current covariance-law consistency does not itself certify posterior or numerical-ODE accuracy.
problems.existing_correction_status: Consistent covariance construction is already present in the current author release and the retained reproduction branch.
problems.impact_rationale: A current author correction clears this item; it does not contribute to paper severity.
